questionTextExtracted: The prices of three commodities A, B, and C are ₹x, y, and z per unit respectively. Person P purchases 4 units of B and sells 2 units of A and 5 units of C. Person Q purchases 2 units of C and sells 3 units of A and 1 unit of B. Person R purchases 1 unit of A and sells 3 units of B and 1 unit of C. In the process P, Q, and R earn ₹15,000, ₹1,000, and ₹4,000 respectively. Find the prices per unit of A, B, and C using the matrix inversion method.

steps: Let x, y, z denote the prices in rupees of one unit of A, B, C.
Profit equals sales revenue minus purchase cost.
The determinant of M is 68, not zero, so M is invertible.
Solving by M⁻¹ gives x=2000, y=1000, z=3000.
